artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $W$ be a Weyl group of type $A$ (i.e. a symmetric group $S_n$) with its standard set of simple reflections, length function $\ell$, and Bruhat order $\le$. For $u\le v$ in $W$, let $[u,v]=\{w\in W : u\le w\le v\}$ denote the Bruhat interval, and let $P_{u,v}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q]$ denote the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial.

Recall the following combinatorial constructions, defined purely in terms of the poset $[u,v]$:

1. (Diamond completeness) An interval $[u,z]\subseteq[u,v]$ is called diamond complete if, whenever $w\in[u,z]$ and $w'\in[u,v]$ cover $w$ in Bruhat order with $w'\notin[u,z]$, certain "diamond" completion conditions force the existence of corresponding elements in $[u,z]$.

2. (Hypercube cluster) For $w\in[u,v]$, let $U(w)$ denote the set of atoms above $w$ in $[u,v]$ (the elements covering $w$). One says that $U(w)$ spans a hypercube cluster if the order ideal generated by $U(w)$ in $[w,v]$ is isomorphic to the Boolean lattice $2^{|U(w)|}$ (a hypercube), with the Hasse diagram structure inherited from Bruhat order.

3. (Hypercube decomposition) An interval $[u,z]\subseteq[u,v]$ is called a hypercube decomposition of $[u,v]$ if $[u,z]$ is diamond complete and $U(w)$ spans a hypercube cluster for every $w\in[u,z]$.

Given a hypercube decomposition $[u,z]$ of $[u,v]$, one defines a polynomial $\widetilde P_{u,v,z}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q]$ by an explicit recursion that uses only the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of strictly smaller subintervals together with the combinatorial data of the hypercube decomposition.

Question: Is it true that for every $u\le v$ in $W$ and every hypercube decomposition $[u,z]$ of $[u,v]$,
$$P_{u,v}(q)=\widetilde P_{u,v,z}(q)\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (known as the BBDVW conjecture) is open in general for the symmetric group. It has been verified for the standard hypercube decomposition via geometric representation theory, and a 2024–2025 preprint proves it for lower intervals $[e,v]$, described as the first non-trivial class of intervals for which it is established. The full conjecture for arbitrary Bruhat intervals in type $A$ remains open.

status_evidence.title: The BBDVW Conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of lower intervals
status_evidence.snippet: We prove the BBDVW Conjecture for lower intervals, the first non-trivial class of intervals for which it has been established.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proved for lower intervals but remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Parabolic recursions for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials and the hypercube decomposition
status_evidence.snippet: Algebraic proof of the hypercube formula via parabolic recursion, generalized to finite Coxeter systems.
status_evidence.claim: The standard hypercube decomposition satisfies the formula, proven via representation-theoretic methods, but this does not resolve the conjecture for arbitrary hypercube decompositions.

status_evidence.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig R-polynomials, combinatorial invariance, and hypercube decompositions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of combinatorial invariance via hypercube decompositions.
status_evidence.claim: Active area; full conjecture not yet established.
